title: What is known about 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE0RF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE0RF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. This machine is the table of DeepMind's busycoq PR 93 (a halting proof for 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0RD---) with that table's halt moved: it goes on where PR 93's machine halts, and it halts only at a three-step detour when a 1 sits next to it. Lean proves 44 of PR 93's macro rules for it; PR 93's engine runs it 7,889,000 fast steps, to a tape of about 22764 cells, without a halt (trusted computation).
Lean proves no halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps (the first 10,000 by the kernel alone), 8 shift rules of the sweeps, the detour and the 44 engine rules.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 32,838 cells have been visited and 25,123 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.506). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.15).

claims.title: 8 shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: For every n and every tape around: A crosses 110101010 rightward writing 001111111, D crosses it leftward writing 111011101 (eight proved rules over its rotations). Each is a theorem steps (s·n) … = some … found and proved by tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py.

claims.title: Where a halt can happen (closed tape language, 5-cell windows)
claims.text: The closure search of bbtools.ctl with windows of 5 cells is closed but allows halts; the halting abstract configurations constrain the neighbourhood of a halt: a halt (C reading 1) needs 11100 or 11111 to the left; any right side starting with 1. A Python check, not a Lean certificate (the Lean library only has the right-edge and no-halt corollaries, which do not apply).

claims.title: Macro structure: bouncer with a sorted list of blocks 1^(6j+1)
claims.text: Left of the start: (110 10 10 10) repeated, a √t bouncer (proved shift rules). Right of it, on the slow side (394 cells after 109 steps), a list of blocks of 1s separated by 00 whose settled lengths are 6j + 1, sorted, with 6j + 5 blocks at group boundaries, e.g. at step 945,073,674: 41 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 7 : 1 : 47 : 49 : 49 : 11 : 1 : 53 : 55 : 59 : 5 : 1 : 1 : 3 : 1 (run lengths, : = 00).

claims.title: No halt in the first 8.29×10<sup>13</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 8.29×1013 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 6 checkpoints, the last at 1.01×1010 steps. Of these steps, the part after the last checkpoint rests on the simulator alone, including 7,944 trip-level jumps: a jump applies many identical round trips at once after seeing the same tape shape recur with constant count changes, which is validated against direct simulation but not proved.

claims.title: PR 93's table with its halt moved, and the detour
claims.text: Mirrored, with the states renamed (A→C, B→D, C→E, D→A, E→B), this machine is the source table T3 = 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1RA0LE_0LB0LF_0LB--- of DeepMind's busycoq PR 93 (which proves that 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0RD--- halts), started in the same state C, with two changes: T3's halt F1 becomes T3's own E1 move (0LF), and T3's one step at D reading 0 becomes a three-step detour. In this machine's orientation the detour is B reading 0: with 0 next to it, three steps end exactly where PR 93's one step ends (detour); with 1 next to it, C reads that 1 and the machine halts (detour_halt). That is its only way to halt.

claims.title: 44 macro rules of PR 93's engine hold for this machine
claims.text: PR 93's 21 basic macro rules, its 5 rules at the blank end, its 8 rules for the DefWord words and its two fast right sweeps, each stated in this machine's orientation for every count and every tape around (some split into the cases count = 0 and count ≥ 1). Their runs never meet the detour's halting case, so the engine's fast steps never hide a halt: a halt can only happen in one of its raw single steps. Generated by py/pr93rules.py with tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py; py/rulecheck.py checks the engine's shift scans the same way.

claims.title: No halt in 7,889,000 fast steps of PR 93's engine (tape about 2<sup>2764</sup> cells)
claims.text: PR 93's engine, extracted to OCaml with only its source table changed (T3 with F1 := 0LF), runs this machine's mirror from blank tape, and engine/watch tests at every fast step whether the next steps reach the halting pattern. None does in the first 7,889,000 fast steps, at the end of which the tape holds about 22764 cells (so about 101663 or more steps). At fast step 2,452,241 (tape about 21400 cells) the run reaches the configuration where PR 93's machine halts (F reading 1); this machine goes on there. The engine agrees with direct simulation through fast step 1,331 (3·1011 steps; in the first 3.6·109 of them all 453,682,544 steps of B reading 0 have 0 next to them). The extracted engine is not a proof for this table: PR 93's soundness proof is for T3.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. C reading 1 halts. The 5-cell closed language allows that with 11100/11111 on the left and any right window starting with 1.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0RF_0LC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LA_1RA1RD_0RD0RF up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1LE0LF_0RA---_0LB0LF up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE---_1LA1LE_0RA0RF up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same tapes at another pace, whatever the states, as 2 other holdouts (listed on the explainer page).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine is a close relative of one that DeepMind proved halts: the same table, mirrored and renamed, with the halt moved. It goes on where its relative stops, and it can only stop at a small detour. This page runs the real machine in your browser and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in 7,889,000 fast steps of PR 93's engine, past the point where PR 93's machine halts.
PR 93's macro rules, proved in Lean for this machine.
No halt in the C simulator; 32,838 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

facts.text: No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 1.01×10<sup>10</sup> steps).

sections.heading: What the machine does: bouncer with a sorted list of blocks 1^(6j+1)
html: Left of the start: (110 10 10 10) repeated, a √t bouncer (proved shift rules). Right of it, on the slow side (394 cells after 109 steps), a list of blocks of 1s separated by 00 whose settled lengths are 6j + 1, sorted, with 6j + 5 blocks at group boundaries, e.g. at step 945,073,674: 41 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 7 : 1 : 47 : 49 : 49 : 11 : 1 : 53 : 55 : 59 : 5 : 1 : 1 : 3 : 1 (run lengths, : = 00).

The first records coincide with those of 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0RD--- (same block lists, different step counts: the two machines share the mechanism with different costs per pass); after a while the two runs diverge but keep the same structure.

sections.heading: A halting proof for the next table over, and where this machine leaves it
html: DeepMind's busycoq PR 93 proves that 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0RD--- halts. Its proof runs a fast engine: an evaluator over run-length tapes of a few macro words (D n = 1 (11)n 00, S n = 1 (01)n+1 and some longer ones), whose every step is a macro rule proved in Coq. The engine works on a source table T3, mirrored and renamed. This machine is T3 too, started in the same state, with two differences.

The halt is moved. T3 halts when F reads 1. T3's states E and F have the same row apart from that, so here they are one state, and where T3 halts this machine does what T3's E does and goes on. In the engine's run that moment comes at fast step 2,452,241, on a tape of about 21400 cells.

One step becomes a detour. Where T3 writes a 1 and turns, this machine first steps over, looks at the next cell, and comes back: three steps that end exactly where T3's one step ends, unless the cell it looked at holds a 1, and then it halts. That is its only halt:

tape (this machine's orientation)steps
PR 93's machine, B reads 0x B>0 0 → D>x 1 01
this machine, 0 next to itx B>0 0 → x 1 C>0 → x D>1 0 → D>x 1 03
this machine, 1 next to itx B>0 1 → x 1 C>1 → halt1

The engine's rules never take the bad branch. Lean proves 44 of the engine's macro rules for this machine itself (lean/PR93Rules.lean), for every count and every tape around; so inside a fast step nothing can halt, and a halt could only come at one of the engine's rare raw single steps. With the source table changed, the engine runs this machine; a check at every fast step looks for the halting pattern.

Result so far. No halt in 7,889,000 fast steps, at which point the tape holds about 22764 cells (trusted computation; the engine agrees with direct simulation through 3·1011 steps). The question stays open: the run would have to go on forever, and nothing yet says why the bad branch never comes.

sections.heading: What a halt would require
html: C reading 1 halts. The 5-cell closed language allows that with 11100/11111 on the left and any right window starting with 1.

sections.heading: What is proved, and what is not
html:
• Sweeps (lean/Sweeps.lean, kernel): A crosses 110101010 rightward writing 001111111, D crosses it leftward writing 111011101 (eight proved rules over its rotations); for every number of copies and every tape around.
  • Bounded run (lean/Blank.lean): no halt in 107 steps (native), 10,000 (kernel); the halting transition is the only way to stop.
  • Detour (lean/Detour.lean, kernel): the only difference from PR 93's table that matters, and its halting case.
  • PR 93's rules (lean/PR93Rules.lean, kernel): 44 macro rules of DeepMind's engine, for this machine.
The engine run is a trusted computation, and the rest of this page is observation of simulated runs (heuristic). Nothing here decides halting.

sections.heading: What would move it forward
html: Find why the engine's raw steps never meet the detour's bad case: the halting pattern needs three 0s between a 1 and the head. In the samples taken (every 1,000th fast step) the tape never has more than two 0s in a row between 1s; longer runs of 0s appear only for a few steps, in the engine's raw stretches at irregular events, and so far always without the 1 beyond them. A proof that they never line up would decide the machine (it would never halt); a counterexample in the run would make it halt.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.506). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.15).
After 109 steps the tape spans 32,838 cells (23,688 left of the start, 394 right), with a density of 1s of 0.765.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0RF_0LC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LA_1RA1RD_0RD0RF: rename A→E, B→A, C→B, D→C, E→D, F→F; it is this table started in state B
  • 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1LE0LF_0RA---_0LB0LF: rename A→C, B→D, C→E, D→A, E→B, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state D, in a mirror
  • 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE---_1LA1LE_0RA0RF: rename A→B, B→C, C→D, D→E, E→A, F→F; it is this table started in state E

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

  • 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0RD---: 8,004,077 configurations, the last at step 10,000,000 here and step 8,004,076 there
  • 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LE_1LC0RF_0RD---: 8,004,077 configurations, the last at step 10,000,000 here and step 8,004,076 there

summary: PR 93's table with its halt moved: it goes on where PR 93's machine halts and can halt only at a 3-step detour; 44 engine rules in Lean, no halt in 7,889,000 fast steps (tape 2^2764); open.
